title: The Grateful Dead Live at Capital Centre on 1982-09-15

ai_review.summary: Matrix recording of a high‑energy 1982 show with killer Playin’/Crazy Fingers jams, the debut Touch of Grey, and solid sound despite an uneven start.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its fire‑cracker first set, the seamless Playin’ > Crazy Fingers combo, standout moments like Let It Grow, Sailor > Saint of Circumstance, a soaring Good Lovin’, and the historic first live Touch of Grey. The soundboard‑plus‑audience (matrix) source is generally good—clear and crisp once it settles, though listeners note some roughness at the very beginning. Overall the show’s musical excitement outweighs the minor recording hiccups.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong consensus of high‑energy performance and many standout songs; recording is mostly clear with only early‑set issues, yielding a solid combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix of soundboard and audience captures the band well after the first few minutes; early portion described as rough/muddy but clears up into crisp, balanced sound.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A unique, bouncy first set driven by the Playin'/Crazy Fingers motif; second set maintains momentum with strong jams and a high‑energy finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers cite his “noodles,” tearing it up on Shakedown, and superb solos on Let It Grow and other jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s playing is highlighted as confident and gel‑like for this era; a few comments note him struggling through Shakedown but overall praised.
band_member_comments.Drums: Pre‑drum segment called “sick” by one reviewer, indicating strong percussion work.
